day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini (€14), then connect to your hotel via metro or bus.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort, check in, and settle into your room. Grab a quick late-night bite near the hotel before resting up for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Quick stop at a late-night kebab or pizza al taglio shop near the hotel (€5–8). Many Roman street food spots stay open past midnight.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Pre-book your Leonardo Express ticket online to save time at the airport. Have €20–25 in cash ready for transport and a snack. Don't forget to validate your train/metro ticket before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Roman adventure with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then head to the Colosseum and Palatine Hill area. Book a combined Colosseum + Roman Forum + Palatine Hill ticket online in advance (€18 full price) to skip the queues. Spend the morning exploring the iconic Colosseum interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across to the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill — your ticket covers all three sites. Wander through the ancient ruins at your own pace and enjoy panoramic views of Rome from Palatine Hill. Alternatively, if budget allows, consider the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour for a guided experience with expert context.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the nearby Testaccio neighborhood, one of Rome's most authentic and budget-friendly districts. Explore the Testaccio Market area and enjoy the lively local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bar — grab a cornetto and cappuccino, the classic Roman breakfast (€2–4 standing at the bar counter)
meals.lunch: Picnic near the Roman Forum — buy fresh bread, cheese, and cured meats from a local alimentari (deli) for under €8. Eat on a bench in the Circus Maximus park.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Remo in Testaccio — a beloved no-frills Roman pizzeria. Try the thin-crust Roman pizza. Budget around €10–14 per person including a house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum tickets at least 2–3 days in advance online to avoid sold-out slots and long queues. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 5–8 km today. Carry a refillable water bottle; Rome's 'nasoni' public fountains offer free, clean drinking water throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — one of the world's greatest art collections. Book your timed-entry ticket online in advance (€17–20) to avoid the notoriously long lines. Arrive right at opening time (9:00 AM) for the best experience. Allow 3–4 hours to explore the galleries and Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit into St. Peter's Square and visit St. Peter's Basilica for free — one of the most magnificent churches in the world. Climb to the top of St. Peter's dome for sweeping views of Rome (€8 with elevator, €6 on foot). Afterward, stroll across the Tiber to the Castel Sant'Angelo exterior (free to view from outside).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Prati neighborhood near the Vatican — a great area for an affordable dinner away from tourist traps. Window-shop along Via Cola di Rienzo.

meals.breakfast: Bar San Calisto or a local bar near the hotel — cornetto and cappuccino (€2–4)
meals.lunch: Forno Feliziani or a local bakery near the Vatican for a quick, cheap lunch — pizza bianca, supplì (fried rice balls), or a panino (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — authentic Roman cuisine with cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara, and house wine at very reasonable prices. Budget €15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except the last Sunday of the month when entry is free but extremely crowded). Wednesday mornings often feature a Papal Audience in St. Peter's Square — check the Vatican website for free tickets if interested. Dress code required for the Basilica: covered shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery Art Experience — one of Rome's most intimate and stunning galleries housing Bernini's extraordinary sculptures and Caravaggio masterpieces. Reservations are mandatory and timed (2-hour slots); book online well in advance (€15–20). Arrive 15 minutes early as late arrivals may be denied entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a free walk through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's version of Central Park. Rent a rowboat on the small lake (€3–5) or simply relax under the trees. Walk or take the scenic tram down to the Trevi Fountain and toss a coin for good luck (free). Then explore the Spanish Steps nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric streets of the historic center. Visit the Pantheon (free exterior; small entry fee of €5 for interior) and the lively Piazza Navona — free to visit and great for people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and espresso at a local bar near the hotel (€2–4)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up supplies from a nearby alimentari or supermarket. Fresh fruit, cheese, and bread for under €8.
meals.dinner: Trattoria dal Cavalier Gino near the Pantheon — a hidden gem with classic Roman pasta dishes like amatriciana and carbonara. Cash only, no sign on the door. Budget €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery limits visitors to 360 per 2-hour slot — book as early as possible, ideally 2–4 weeks ahead. The gallery is a 15-minute walk from the nearest metro (Spagna). Trevi Fountain is best visited early morning or late evening to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Trastevere neighborhood — one of Rome's most picturesque and authentic districts. Visit the stunning Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free entry, 12th-century mosaics are breathtaking). Wander the cobblestone streets and soak in the neighborhood's bohemian charm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Tiber to the Jewish Ghetto area and visit the ancient Teatro di Marcello (free exterior view) and the ruins of the Portico d'Ottavia. Then head to Campo de' Fiori market (open until about 2 PM) for fresh produce, local cheeses, and street food snacks. Spend the late afternoon at the Largo di Torre Argentina — free ancient Roman ruins where Julius Caesar was assassinated.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere for dinner and the vibrant Friday evening atmosphere. The neighborhood comes alive at night with locals and travelers alike.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast at a Trastevere bar — try Bar San Calisto, a beloved local institution with very cheap prices (espresso €1, cornetto €1)
meals.lunch: Street food at Campo de' Fiori market or a nearby alimentari. Try suppli, porchetta sandwiches, or a slice of pizza al taglio (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — a classic Roman trattoria with excellent cacio e pepe and tiramisu. Very popular, arrive early or expect a wait. Budget €15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Trastevere is very walkable and best explored on foot. Friday evenings can be quite busy, so arrive at restaurants by 7:30 PM to avoid long waits. The neighborhood is also a great spot for a budget aperitivo — many bars offer free snacks with a €5–7 drink.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to the Aventine Hill — a peaceful, less-touristy area with stunning views. Visit the famous Knights of Malta Keyhole (free) for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Explore the beautiful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with panoramic views over Rome. Visit the Basilica di Santa Sabina (free entry, one of Rome's oldest churches).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the lively Porta Portese flea market (open Saturday mornings until 2 PM — catch the tail end) or explore the Ostiense district for street art and local culture. Visit the Pyramid of Cestius (free exterior) — a surprising ancient Egyptian-style pyramid in the middle of Rome. Explore the Non-Catholic Cemetery nearby (€3 suggested donation), where Keats and Shelley are buried.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening in the lively Testaccio or Pigneto neighborhood — both known for authentic local nightlife and great value dining. Enjoy a leisurely passeggiata (evening stroll) like a true Roman.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick bar stop near the hotel (€2–4)
meals.lunch: Testaccio Market food stalls — try supplì, artichokes alla romana, and local street food. One of the best and most affordable food markets in Rome (€8–12 for a full spread)
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — a beloved trattoria built into the Monte dei Cocci (a hill made of ancient pottery shards). Excellent Roman classics at fair prices. Budget €15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a great day to mingle with locals. The Porta Portese flea market is Rome's largest and most famous — go early (before 10 AM) for the best finds and fewer crowds. Carry small bills and practice your bargaining. Sunscreen and a hat are recommended for outdoor sightseeing in June.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning revisiting your favorite spots or discovering hidden gems you may have missed. Consider a free visit to one of Rome's stunning free churches: San Luigi dei Francesi (Caravaggio paintings), Sant'Ignazio di Loyola (incredible trompe-l'oeil ceiling), or Santa Maria della Vittoria (Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa). All are free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at budget-friendly spots — avoid tourist traps near major monuments. Head to a local supermarket (Conad, Carrefour) or market for authentic Italian food souvenirs: dried pasta, olive oil, pesto, and local snacks at a fraction of tourist shop prices. Pack your bags and check out of the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final farewell dinner in Rome before heading to the airport or resting for an early departure. Raise a glass of local house wine to an unforgettable Roman adventure.

meals.breakfast: Last Roman bar breakfast — splurge slightly on a proper sit-down breakfast at a nice café. Try Café Sant'Eustachio near the Pantheon, famous for its exceptional coffee (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local trattoria or pizza al taglio spot — keep it simple and affordable (€8–12). Try a classic Roman supplì and a slice of pizza bianca for a perfect send-off.
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite restaurant from the week, or try Osteria Bonelli in the Prenestino neighborhood for an ultra-local, no-frills Roman feast at rock-bottom prices. Budget €12–15 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: If your flight departs from Fiumicino, allow at least 1.5–2 hours for the journey from central Rome (Leonardo Express from Termini, €14). For Ciampino airport, take the Terravision or SIT bus (€6–8) from Termini. Keep a small amount of euros for transport and tips. Consider purchasing a 48-hour or 72-hour Roma Pass (€28–38) if you haven't already — it covers public transport and some museum entries.

day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite near the hotel if hungry — look for a 24-hour bar or pizzeria al taglio (pizza by the slice) open late, budget ~€10–15

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 22:30, so Day 1 is purely arrival and settling in. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid late-night hassle. Keep luggage light for easy navigation. Set an alarm to start Day 2 refreshed and early.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then take a gentle orientation walk around your neighborhood to get your bearings. Stroll along the nearest riverside promenade or piazza to soak in the Roman atmosphere and shake off any jet lag.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Borghese Gallery Art Experience — one of Rome's most intimate and stunning galleries housing Bernini's extraordinary sculptures and Caravaggio masterpieces. Note: reservations are mandatory and timed, so book the 14:00 slot in advance. Spend 2 hours immersed in world-class art in a manageable, crowd-friendly setting.
day_by_day.evening: Wind down with a passeggiata (evening stroll) through the Villa Borghese gardens, then head to the Prati neighborhood for dinner — a relaxed, local area near the Vatican with excellent mid-range trattorias.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bar — cornetto and cappuccino, ~€5–8
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the hotel — try a tramezzino (Italian sandwich) or suppli (fried rice balls), ~€10–15
meals.dinner: Trattoria Pizzarium or similar in Prati — Roman-style thin-crust pizza or pasta, ~€20–30 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery strictly limits visitors to 2 hours and requires advance booking — book online at least 2–3 weeks ahead. Wear comfortable shoes for the garden walk. Gallery is closed Mondays, so Tuesday is perfect.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — arrive at opening time (08:00) with a pre-booked skip-the-line ticket to beat the crowds. Spend 3–4 hours exploring the vast collections of ancient sculptures, Renaissance maps, and tapestries, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit through St. Peter's Square and visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry) — climb the dome for panoramic views over Rome if energy allows (~€8 by stairs). Afterward, rest in the shade of the colonnade before heading toward Castel Sant'Angelo for exterior photos and a riverside walk.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — wander through cobblestone streets sampling local Roman street food including supplì, artichokes, pecorino, and local wines. A perfect immersive introduction to Roman food culture.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before Vatican — grab a cornetto and espresso at a bar near the museum entrance, ~€5
meals.lunch: Lunch in Prati near the Vatican — Il Sorpasso or similar wine bar with antipasti and cold cuts, ~€18–25
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk (street food tastings) — supplement with a glass of local wine at a Trastevere enoteca, ~€10–15 extra

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums can be overwhelming — focus on the Raphael Rooms and Sistine Chapel if time is short. The food walk typically runs 3 hours starting around 18:30–19:00; confirm exact meeting point when booking. Wear very comfortable walking shoes — cobblestones in Trastevere are charming but uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class — start your morning at the vibrant market selecting fresh seasonal ingredients with a local chef. Learn to cook 3–4 traditional Roman dishes (cacio e pepe, carciofi alla romana, tiramisu) in a hands-on class. This is a highlight for any food lover.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class lunch (usually included), take a leisurely afternoon to explore the surrounding historic center on foot — visit the nearby Piazza Navona with Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, then wander to the Pantheon (book timed entry online, ~€5). Enjoy gelato from a quality gelateria like Giolitti.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening to revisit favorite spots or explore independently. Consider an aperitivo hour — a classic Roman pre-dinner ritual with a spritz or Negroni and complimentary snacks at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the market — bar espresso and pastry, ~€5
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class (you eat what you cook!) — one of the best meals of the trip
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near Piazza Navona — try Osteria dell'Enoteca or a neighborhood trattoria for Roman classics like rigatoni all'amatriciana, ~€25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Campo de' Fiori market runs until about 13:00 — the cooking class typically starts at 10:00. Book well in advance as classes fill up quickly. The Pantheon now requires timed-entry tickets; book online to avoid queues. Stay hydrated — June in Rome can be warm (25–32°C).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Colosseum and surrounding ancient monuments — book a skip-the-line combo ticket (Colosseum + Roman Forum + Palatine Hill) online in advance. Spend the morning exploring the iconic amphitheater with an audio guide or small group tour for context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue with the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour — explore the ancient ruins of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill with a knowledgeable local guide as the afternoon light turns golden. See the Temple of Saturn, Arch of Titus, and sweeping views over the ancient city. The late afternoon light makes this especially magical for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's original working-class food district and the birthplace of cucina romana. Browse the covered market (if still open) and settle in for dinner at one of the authentic local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — fuel up well before a day of walking, ~€8–12
meals.lunch: Packed snack or quick bite near the Colosseum — avoid tourist trap restaurants; try a nearby alimentari for a panino, ~€8–12
meals.dinner: Testaccio trattoria — try Da Remo for Roman pizza or Flavio al Velavevodetto for offal-free Roman classics like coda alla vaccinara, ~€25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum area is extremely busy on Fridays — arrive at opening (09:00) or book the sunset tour slot. Comfortable shoes are essential as the Forum has uneven ancient stone paths. Bring a hat and sunscreen for the open-air ruins. The guided sunset tour typically runs 17:00–19:30.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Ghetto and Largo di Torre Argentina (the ancient ruins where Julius Caesar was assassinated, now home to a cat sanctuary — free to visit). Wander through the atmospheric medieval streets of the Ghetto and visit the Great Synagogue of Rome (museum entry ~€12).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Tiber for an afternoon in Trastevere in daylight — visit the stunning Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free, beautiful golden mosaics), browse artisan shops, and relax in the piazza with a coffee. This is a great neighborhood for independent art and craft gallery hopping.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner for your second-to-last evening — choose a well-reviewed osteria in Trastevere or the historic center for a multi-course Roman feast with local wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bar in the Jewish Ghetto area — try a maritozzo (cream-filled bun), a Roman specialty, ~€6–8
meals.lunch: Lunch in Trastevere — Da Enzo al 29 or similar beloved local trattoria for cacio e pepe and carciofi, ~€20–28
meals.dinner: Elevated dinner at a mid-range osteria — try Grazia & Graziella or Tonnarello in Trastevere, ~€35–45 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Trastevere is lively but can be crowded by evening — aim to arrive for dinner by 19:30 to secure a table without a long wait (or book ahead). The Jewish Ghetto bakeries sell incredible Jewish-Roman pastries like crostata di ricotta e visciole — don't miss them.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit the Porta Portese flea market (Rome's famous Sunday market, open 06:00–14:00) for last-minute souvenirs, vintage finds, and local color. Alternatively, if you prefer a quieter close, revisit a favorite spot — perhaps the Pincian Hill overlook above Piazza del Popolo for a sweeping farewell view of Rome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely farewell lunch, then return to the hotel to collect luggage and begin your departure journey. Allow ample time for Rome's traffic, especially on Sunday afternoons.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or transfer to airport/next destination. Reflect on a wonderful week of art, food, and la dolce vita.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast — sit down at a classic café for a proper espresso and cornetto, savoring the ritual one last time, ~€5–8
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch near the hotel or in a favorite neighborhood — choose something meaningful, perhaps a dish you loved earlier in the week, ~€20–30
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or an early dinner if departure time allows

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese is cash-only and very busy — go early (before 09:00) for the best experience and less crowding. Keep your belongings secure in market crowds. If your flight departs in the evening, consider storing luggage at Termini station (left luggage service available) to free up your last afternoon. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before flight departure for airport transfer and check-in.

meals.lunch: N/A – In transit

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in preparation so your room is fully ready upon arrival. Keep Day 1 completely relaxed – no scheduled excursions. Store luggage immediately and prioritize rest for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort, then a scenic drive into central Rome. Begin your Roman holiday with an exclusive skip-the-line Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel experience. A private expert art historian guide will lead you through the Gallery of Maps, the Raphael Rooms, and finally into Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel. With a private tour, you'll gain access before general crowds and enjoy an intimate, unhurried experience among one of the world's greatest art collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, stroll across the Tiber via the Ponte Sant'Angelo, pausing to admire Castel Sant'Angelo. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a refined restaurant in Prati neighborhood. Afterward, explore the elegant Via della Conciliazione and the grandeur of St. Peter's Square at your own pace. Optional: ascend to the top of St. Peter's Basilica dome for panoramic views over Rome (included in your guide's itinerary).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a brief rest and sunset aperitivo on your private terrace. Dress for dinner and head to one of Rome's celebrated fine-dining establishments for a multi-course tasting menu showcasing modern Roman cuisine paired with sommelier-selected Italian wines.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – freshly baked cornetti, seasonal fruit, eggs cooked to order, cold cuts, and barista-prepared espresso or cappuccino.
meals.lunch: Ristorante Il Sorpasso (Prati) – an upscale Roman trattoria celebrated for elevated classics: cacio e pepe, artichoke alla giudia, and excellent natural wines. Reserve a terrace table.
meals.dinner: La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri) – Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant. Chef Heinz Beck's legendary tasting menu with panoramic city views and an extraordinary 60,000-bottle wine cellar. Advance reservation essential; smart dress code required.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican private tour well in advance – early morning entry (8:00 AM) is strongly recommended to avoid crowds. La Pergola reservations should be secured months ahead. Private car and driver recommended for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Start with breakfast at the resort, then head to the Borghese Gallery Art Experience – one of Rome's most exclusive and intimate galleries. Entry is strictly timed and limited to 360 visitors per session, making it feel genuinely private. Your expert guide will illuminate Bernini's extraordinary marble sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks. Afterward, take a peaceful stroll through the surrounding Villa Borghese gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Villa Borghese, descend into the Spanish Steps area for a refined afternoon. Browse the luxury boutiques along Via Condotti (Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi) for optional shopping. Visit the Trevi Fountain and the Pantheon at a leisurely pace, soaking in the architectural grandeur. Stop at a historic café for a mid-afternoon espresso and pastry.
day_by_day.evening: Embark on the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk – a curated culinary journey through the cobblestone streets of Rome's most atmospheric neighborhood. Sample supplì (Roman fried rice balls), artisan pizza al taglio, aged Pecorino, and local wines poured by passionate producers. Your expert food guide will share the history and culture behind each bite.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – freshly squeezed blood orange juice, Roman-style pastries, yogurt with local honey, and a perfectly pulled double espresso.
meals.lunch: Il Pagliaccio (2 Michelin stars, near the Pantheon) – Chef Anthony Genovese's creative Italian cuisine in an intimate, art-filled setting. Outstanding tasting menu with wine pairing.
meals.dinner: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk serves as dinner – a progressive tasting experience across multiple stops. Conclude the evening with a glass of Cesanese del Piglio red wine at a candlelit Trastevere enoteca.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be reserved weeks in advance – entry slots sell out quickly. The food walk typically runs 3 hours (starting around 6:30–7:00 PM). Wear comfortable walking shoes. Trastevere is magical at dusk – bring a camera.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class experience. Begin at the vibrant Campo de' Fiori morning market alongside your private chef, hand-selecting the finest seasonal produce, fresh pasta, local cheeses, and artisan ingredients. Then transfer to a beautifully appointed cooking studio (or a private Roman apartment kitchen) where you'll learn to prepare a full Roman menu: antipasto, handmade pasta, a secondi, and a classic Roman dessert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the fruits of your culinary labor – sit down to a long, leisurely lunch with wines matched to each course by your chef-instructor. After lunch, return to the resort for a relaxing afternoon. Indulge in the resort's spa facilities: a deep-tissue massage, hydrotherapy, or simply unwind by the pool with a Campari spritz.
day_by_day.evening: A calm, elegant evening. Take a sunset stroll along the waterfront near the resort, then dine at the resort's signature restaurant for a refined dinner showcasing the best of Lazio's coastal and inland ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before the early market departure – espresso, cornetto, and seasonal fruit.
meals.lunch: The cooking class itself culminates in a full sit-down lunch with matched wines – a multi-course Roman feast you prepared with your own hands. Expect cacio e pepe or carbonara, braised meats, and a tiramisu or panna cotta.
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort Signature Restaurant – a refined tasting menu featuring Lazio ingredients: sea bass from the Tyrrhenian coast, local lamb, black truffle from Norcia, and an expertly curated Italian wine list. Dine on the terrace under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Campo de' Fiori market is most vibrant between 7:30–9:00 AM – arrive early for the best selection. The cooking class typically runs 4–5 hours including the lunch. The afternoon spa session should be pre-booked with the resort concierge. A perfect mid-trip reset day.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a private half-day excursion to Ostia Antica – Rome's remarkably preserved ancient port city, often overshadowed by Pompeii but equally stunning. With a private archaeologist guide, explore the mosaics, amphitheater, baths, and ancient taverns of this atmospheric site. Being close to the resort's coastal location, this is an ideal and convenient excursion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Rome for an afternoon dedicated to the Capitoline Museums – the world's oldest public museums, housing iconic works including the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and sweeping views over the Roman Forum. A private guide will bring the collections to life with expert storytelling.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour – the crown jewel of the day. As the golden hour light bathes the ancient stones, your expert local guide leads an exclusive after-hours sunset tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Walk where emperors lived, see the Temple of Saturn glow in amber light, and watch the sun dip behind the Colosseum from the heights of Palatine Hill. An utterly unforgettable Roman experience.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – eggs Benedict with local prosciutto, freshly baked bread, seasonal fruit platter, and freshly brewed Italian coffee.
meals.lunch: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio (near the Pantheon) – a beloved Roman institution serving exceptional traditional Roman cuisine. Try the oxtail (coda alla vaccinara) or the abbacchio al forno. Elegant, unhurried, and deeply authentic.
meals.dinner: Aroma Restaurant (rooftop, next to the Colosseum) – dine with a direct, breathtaking view of the illuminated Colosseum. Chef Giuseppe Di Iorio's refined Roman cuisine elevated to Michelin-starred heights. The ultimate Rome dining experience. Reserve the best terrace table well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The sunset tour timing should align with the actual sunset (approximately 8:30–9:00 PM in June 2027) – coordinate with your guide. Aroma Restaurant is immediately adjacent, making the transition from tour to dinner seamless and spectacular. Private car recommended for the full day.

day_by_day.morning: A leisurely, unstructured morning at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast on your private terrace overlooking the sea, and take a morning swim in the Tyrrhenian. This is your free morning to decompress and soak in the luxury of your surroundings. Optional: a morning yoga session or a personal training session arranged by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private day trip to Castelli Romani – the volcanic hill towns south of Rome beloved by Roman aristocracy for centuries. Visit Frascati for a private wine tasting at a historic estate, explore the gardens of Villa Aldobrandini, and wander through the charming hilltop village of Nemi, famous for its wild strawberries (fragole di bosco). A private driver and guide make this an effortless and luxurious excursion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a final grand evening in the city. Enjoy a pre-dinner Negroni at a celebrated rooftop bar (Hotel de la Ville or Minerva Roof Garden) watching Rome's golden skyline glow at dusk. Then proceed to dinner at one of Rome's most storied restaurants for a celebratory final fine-dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Extended, indulgent resort breakfast on your private terrace – the full spread, enjoyed slowly with sea views and morning sunshine.
meals.lunch: Frascati wine estate lunch – a curated farm-to-table lunch paired with estate-produced Frascati Superiore white wines. Fresh pasta, roasted meats, local vegetables, and dessert in a centuries-old cellar or garden setting.
meals.dinner: Il Convivio Troiani (near Piazza Navona) – one of Rome's most celebrated fine-dining institutions, helmed by the Troiani brothers for over 30 years. A 1-Michelin-star restaurant with a legendary wine list and a deeply personal, creative Roman tasting menu. The perfect penultimate dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Castelli Romani wine estate lunch in advance – many estates require reservations and offer private tastings for premium guests. The rooftop aperitivo bars fill quickly on Saturday evenings – arrive by 7:00 PM for the best views. This is a beautifully balanced day of relaxation and exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome. After a leisurely last breakfast at the resort, take one final stroll along the waterfront or through the resort gardens. Pack and check out at your leisure (arrange a late check-out with the concierge – typically available for premium guests). Make a last visit to a beloved spot: perhaps the Pantheon at opening hour (9:00 AM on Sundays) when it is serene and magnificent, or simply linger over an espresso at a historic café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, enjoy a final Roman lunch at a classic neighborhood trattoria. Afterward, your private luxury transfer will collect you from the resort or city center and deliver you to Fiumicino Airport in style, with ample time before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Rome. Reflect on an extraordinary week of art, cuisine, ancient history, and luxury as you board your flight home, carrying memories of the Eternal City that will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – make it special. Request a private table in the best location, order your favorites from the week, and savor every last sip of Italian espresso.
meals.lunch: Da Enzo al 29 (Trastevere) – a legendary, intimate Roman trattoria serving some of the city's most authentic cacio e pepe, carbonara, and coda alla vaccinara. A perfect, heartfelt final Roman meal. Reserve ahead as it is always in demand.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport. Fiumicino's Terminal 3 has several decent options; alternatively, pack a curated picnic from a Roman deli (salumi, cheeses, taralli, and a small bottle of Brunello) for the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Request late check-out (2:00–3:00 PM) from the resort concierge at the start of your stay to ensure it is guaranteed. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the transfer and check-in at Fiumicino. Consider purchasing artisan food souvenirs (aged Pecorino, bottarga, artisan pasta, truffle products) from Eataly Roma or a local salumeria before departure.
